docRequirement: whats-new/2026-w20.md:87 binds two things: (1) every MCP **stdio** server receives `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` in its spawn environment, "matching hooks"; (2) plugin configs may reference `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` inside `command` (and the other expansion locations). The same contract is stated normatively outside the changelog at `skills.md:307` — `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` is "the same path hooks and MCP servers receive as CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR" — which this repo already cites for skills (packages/shared/src/capabilities/runtime-skill-content.ts:121-127), so the binding does not rest on a what's-new bullet alone.
current:

Plugin stdio branch: packages/shared/src/mcp/runtime-pool-servers.ts:472-478 builds `pluginRuntimeEnvForProfile(...)`, which for `claude-plugin-env-v1` adds `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR: paths.projectPath` (packages/shared/src/plugins/data-paths.ts:132) — and NOTHING else emits any project-dir name: `pluginRuntimeEnv` emits only the four PLUGIN_ROOT/PLUGIN_DATA spellings (data-paths.ts:98-105) and `codexCompatPluginEnv` deliberately none (:111-117). divergence:
Two distinct deltas, one narrowing and one wrong-key.

A. NARROWER (clause 1): the project-dir spawn variable exists for plugin-supplied stdio MCP only. Native sources and project `.mcp.json` stdio servers receive it under neither spelling (client.ts:398). Nothing about the value is wrong — it is absent, and the supply exists one layer away (base-agent.ts:2221).

B. WRONG KEY (clause 2): for a plugin config the VALUE is right and the KEY IS WRONG. `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` in an imported Claude manifest is rewritten to `${NESSY_PROJECT_DIR}` (claude.ts:2710) while the env emits `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` (data-paths.ts:132) — the two halves of the same pair name different variables, so the reference resolves to neither. Fixing this is one emitted name, not a mechanism. For a project `.mcp.json` clause 2 is simply not built: the expansion environment is bare `process.env` (project-config.ts:106).

C. Consequence correction to the filed state: an unresolved reference does NOT "resolve to nothing". `expandConfigVariables` defaults to `unset: 'literal'` (server-config-values.ts:54, :62), so the command keeps the literal text `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/...` and the server is spawned with a bogus path — an ENOENT, not a blank.

change.what: Stop hardcoding the expansion environment. Add an options bag `{ projectDirectory?: string }` to `parseMcpServersDocument` (:180) and thread it into `parseProjectMcpServer` (:89). Replace `const environment = process.env` (:106) with `const environment = projectDirectory ? { ...process.env, NESSY_PROJECT_DIR: projectDirectory, CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR: projectDirectory } : process.env` — host value spread LAST so a stale ambient export cannot win, and both names withheld when the host has no project dir so the existing literal-plus-warning path (:201-203) is byte-identical for a project-less session. Pass `workspaceRootPath` through from `loadProjectMcpServers` (:218-235) for symmetry, but note that function has no production caller; the runtime fix is the next entry.

Add `projectDirectory?: string` to `MaterializePoolServersOptions` (:90-139); pass it from `materializeRuntimePoolServers` (:269-279) into `materializeSnapshotMcpServers` (:431) as a new parameter. Then, inside that function: (a) resource branch (:461-467) — pass `{ projectDirectory }` to `parseMcpServersDocument`, AND when the parsed entry is stdio store `{ ...config, env: { ...projectDirEnv, ...config.env } }` so the process RECEIVES the variable and does not merely expand it (doc clause 1 is about the environment, not the token); (b) native non-plugin stdio branch — seed the same pair at the head of `const environment` (:514-517) so `resolveRuntimeString` over command/args/cwd (:526, :574) and the spawn env (:578-580) both see it. Leave the plugin branch untouched: `pluginRuntimeEnvForProfile` (:472-478) already supplies it there. Define `projectDirEnv` once as `projectDirectory ? { NESSY_PROJECT_DIR: projectDirectory, CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR: projectDirectory } : {}`.

Pass `projectDirectory: this.runtimeSkillProjectDirectory()` in the `materializeRuntimePoolServers` options at :1731-1746. Promote `runtimeSkillProjectDirectory` from `private` to a single internal reader used by BOTH the skill path (:2202) and the MCP path — `skills.md:307` says it is "the same path", so two independent derivations are the drift this repo has already paid for elsewhere.

Pass `projectDirectory` only when the entry has a real project root. Do NOT reuse the `entry.workspaceRootPath ?? entry.workspaceId` fallback at :499 as a path — when it is a workspace id, pass nothing, so the browse pool leaves the token literal and warns instead of spawning against a fabricated directory.

One line: emit `...(paths.projectPath ? { NESSY_PROJECT_DIR: paths.projectPath } : {})`. That is the name claude.ts:2710 rewrites to, the name `schema.ts:282` (`PLUGIN_RUNTIME_PATH_ROOTS`) already accepts as an LSP `workspaceFolder` root, and the name `hook-command.ts:164` already lists as an exec-form placeholder — today all three name a variable nothing sets. Keep `claudeCompatPluginEnv`'s `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` (:132) as the compat alias, which makes its :123-125 comment true. Putting it in `pluginRuntimeEnv` (rather than only in `claudeCompatPluginEnv`) is deliberate: a generic or Codex-profile bundle may legally declare `${NESSY_PROJECT_DIR}` per schema.ts:279-283, and the narrower fix leaves those unresolvable.

Both compare whole records including `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`; add `NESSY_PROJECT_DIR`. Also check packages/shared/src/plugins/__tests__/unified-adapter-conformance.test.ts:568-573, which asserts the Codex profile has no `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` — that assertion stays true and must not be widened to NESSY_PROJECT_DIR.

Two tests, one positive one negative: (1) a project `.mcp.json` stdio entry whose `command` is `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/bin/server` materializes to the absolute path AND the resulting config's `env` carries `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`; (2) with no project directory supplied, the command keeps the literal `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` text and the missing-variable warning still fires (the R17 withhold rule, unchanged). Add a plugin case proving an imported Claude manifest's rewritten `${NESSY_PROJECT_DIR}` now expands.

blastRadius:
Crosses two packages (`shared`, `server-core`) and touches a child-process spawn environment — a trust boundary, so the value must come from the host-validated project root and never from the repo-owned `.mcp.json` document.

- Connection identity: `SdkMcpServerConfig.env` is part of what `mcpConnectionKey` digests (packages/shared/src/mcp/mcp-pool.ts:429-465 passes `config.env` straight through to the client config the pool keys on). Adding a key changes every native stdio server's identity once, so the first `pool.sync` after the change reconnects them. Not a persisted schema, but it is a runtime wire-identity change.
- Precompute/runtime symmetry: packages/shared/src/capabilities/resolver.ts:1437 (`missingRequiredEnvironmentNames`) and runtime-pool-servers.ts:826 (`materializePluginMcpEnvironment`) both call `materializeMcpDescriptorEnvironment` with a `plugin` layer built by `pluginRuntimeEnvForProfile`. Adding a name changes availability verdicts on BOTH sides; they must keep sharing the helper. resolver.ts:1432-1436 records the shipped bug from the last time these two disagreed (a server reported AVAILABLE that the runtime then withheld).

No third: mcp-pool.ts:429-465 forwards config unchanged, and the Claude SDK backend hands the SDK only in-process session tools plus source-proxy servers backed by the same pool.
- Existing tests over the touched readers: packages/shared/src/mcp/__tests__/always-load-config.test.ts, mcp-server-timeout-config.test.ts, oauth-config.test.ts, ws-transport.test.ts, config-variable-expansion.test.ts (all call `parseMcpServersDocument`), packages/shared/tests/mcp-pool.test.ts, packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/base-agent.test.ts:803.
userImpact: A user who writes the documented thing gets a broken server with a near-useless error. Put `"command": "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/scripts/mcp-server.js"` (or `"args": ["${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/..."]`, or an `env` entry) in a repo's `.mcp.json`, open that project, and the entry is spawned with the literal string `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/scripts/mcp-server.js` as the executable — it fails ENOENT and the server shows as failed/disconnected in the MCP/Sources list. The only diagnostic is a debug-channel line, "references unset environment variables with no default", which names the variable but not that the host was supposed to supply it. Separately, any project-scoped stdio server that reads `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` from its own environment (the normal pattern for a repo-local server that must not hardcode a path) sees it undefined and either silently falls back to `cwd` or refuses to start. For imported Claude plugins the same reference fails too, through the wrong-key path — the process does carry `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, but the manifest's token was rewritten to a name nothing sets, so `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` in a plugin's MCP command is broken while reading `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` inside the server works. That split is the most confusing surface here.
